title: Read the query before the index
summary: Design one composite index from a real query and verify it with EXPLAIN.

scenario.briefing: The storefront opens a customer's order history with a status filter, newest first. The current index was copied from a template, and the query still reads far more rows than it returns.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The query filters customer_id and status with equality, then sorts by placed_at.
Order the index columns: equality filters first, the sort column last.
Use INCLUDE (id, total_cents) so the scan can stay inside the index.
Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and look for an Index Only Scan instead of a Seq Scan.

misconceptions.description: Leading the index with the low-cardinality status column.
misconceptions.feedback: Status filters little on its own. Lead with customer_id, which matches far fewer rows, then order the remaining columns by the query.
A plain EXPLAIN shows estimates. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) runs the query and shows actual time and buffer usage.

misconceptions.description: Adding an index for every column.
misconceptions.feedback: Each index costs storage and slows writes. Add indexes for real query shapes and verify them with a plan.

sections.title: Selectivity picks the lead column
sections.body: customer_id matches a small slice of the table; status has only a few values and filters little. Put the more selective equality column first.

sections.title: Composite order follows the query
sections.body: A B-tree can use the index for equality on customer_id and status, then read placed_at in descending order. Put the sort column after the equality columns so PostgreSQL does not need a separate sort.

sections.title: A covering index avoids heap fetches
sections.body: INCLUDE adds id and total_cents to the index leaf, so an index-only scan can answer the query when the visibility map allows it. PostgreSQL secondary indexes do not store the primary key for you, so add id when the query returns it. Each extra column makes the index larger, so include only what the query selects.

sections.title: The plan is evidence
sections.body: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) runs the query and reports actual time, rows, loops, and buffer reads. Compare the plan before and after the index instead of assuming the index is used.

vocabulary.definition: A separate structure that lets the database find rows without scanning the whole table.
How much a column narrows the result; a column with many distinct values is usually more selective.
An index over several columns in a fixed order.
An index that contains every column a query needs, so the table heap is not visited for the selected values.
Reading every row of a table because no index answers the query.
A command that runs a query and reports its actual plan and timing; the BUFFERS option adds buffer usage.

steps.title: Index the order history query
steps.prompt: Edit indexes.sql. Drop the mismatched index and replace it with one that serves the customer and status filter, the newest-first order, and the selected columns. Add an EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) check.

files.content:
-- TODO: replace this index with one built for the query below.
CREATE INDEX orders_status_idx ON orders (status, placed_at DESC);

-- Query: the twenty most recent paid orders for one customer.
SELECT id, placed_at, total_cents
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id = 'c1'
  AND status = 'paid'
ORDER BY placed_at DESC
LIMIT 20;

tests.description: The mismatched index is dropped and replaced with one built for the query.
The index covers the selected columns.
The plan is measured with real timing and buffer counts.
The query keeps its filter, order, and limit.

steps.title: Index design and query plans

statements.label: A column that matches few rows is usually a better leading index column than a column with three distinct values.
In a composite B-tree index, equality columns should come before the column used for ordering.
A covering index lets the planner answer a query without reading the selected columns from the table heap.
A low-cardinality column such as status should always lead a composite index.
EXPLAIN without ANALYZE reports actual execution time and buffer counts.

steps.explanation: The index follows the query: equality columns first, the sort column next, and the selected columns in INCLUDE. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) proves the plan with real time and buffer counts.
